summary: The Toronto Coach Terminal is the central bus station for inter-city services in Toronto, located at 610 Bay Street in Downtown. It is owned by Toronto Coach Terminal Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of the Toronto Transit Commission (TTC). The TTC leased the entire station to Coach Canada and Greyhound Canada on July 8, 2012, after opening in 1931 as the Gray Coach Terminal, an Art Deco building that replaced an earlier open air terminal.
one_line: Toronto's central inter-city bus station at 610 Bay Street, owned by a TTC subsidiary and leased to Coach Canada and Greyhound Canada since 2012.
key_facts: The Toronto Coach Terminal is the central bus station for inter-city services in Toronto, Ontario, Canada.
The Toronto Coach Terminal is located at 610 Bay Street in the city's Downtown.
The Toronto Coach Terminal is owned by Toronto Coach Terminal Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of the Toronto Transit Commission (TTC).
The TTC managed the Toronto Coach Terminal directly until July 8, 2012.
On July 8, 2012, the TTC leased the Toronto Coach Terminal in its entirety to Coach Canada and Greyhound Canada.
The lease of the Toronto Coach Terminal to Coach Canada and Greyhound Canada was for $1.2 million annually.
The Toronto Coach Terminal opened in 1931 as the Gray Coach Terminal.
The Art Deco style Gray Coach Terminal was home base for Gray Coach, an interurban bus service then owned by the TTC.
The Gray Coach Terminal replaced an earlier open air terminal, Gray Line Terminal.
